title: Begin Actual Construction in the New Source Review Preconstruction Permitting Program
pass_4_primary_concern: The proposal is conceptually coherent, but the record leaves the biggest pressure points in baseline support, boundary drawing, and enforceability of the non-emitting-component carveout.
pass_5_concise_why: The proposal is structurally ordinary for an NPRM, but the carveout boundary and the burden story still need sharper support.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: Commenters can still shape how EPA defines the non-emitting carveout, handles reliance, and keeps state-by-state implementation consistent.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: EPA relies on statutory interpretation plus program redesign rather than an enforcement-specific workaround.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to show why the proposed reading is the best statutory fit.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule reads the CAA as allowing more pre-permit construction than the current practice appears to allow.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to identify the text and precedent that support the new reading.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule allows more early work before the permit gate closes, which can shift leverage toward applicants that front-load construction.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask whether later permit discretion remains fully insulated from sunk-cost pressure.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal says the current language creates uncertainty, delays, and regulatory burdens, but the notice text does not fully quantify the claimed problem.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to disclose the project-frequency and cost evidence behind the burden claim.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: EPA's remedy is a broad definition rewrite even though the problem may vary by project type and permitting program.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA whether narrower guidance or model text would solve the same problem.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule depends on permit writers making consistent judgment calls about what counts as non-emitting work.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA for examples and model criteria that permit writers can actually apply.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: EPA says the rule preserves public health and welfare protections, but the notice does not fully show the magnitude of the practical impact tradeoff.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to quantify the retained protections and the remaining risk exposure.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: Applicants could try to use the carveout to lock in site work before later emissions-unit review.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA how it will prevent strategic sequencing around the permit gate.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal relies on a case-by-case approach, but the notice does not yet provide a sufficiently objective safeguard for the non-emitting carveout boundary.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to add examples, exclusions, or model language that make the boundary enforceable.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: EPA acknowledges applicants may build early at their own economic risk, which can still create pressure before final NSR review.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to explain why the risk warning is enough to preserve the review process.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule shifts more activity into the pre-permit phase, so the permit gate must remain clean and enforceable.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA whether the later permit decision is fully insulated from early construction choices.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal separates non-emitting construction from source construction, but the practical consequences of that split are not fully mapped.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to map the consequence classes for common projects.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal is coherent overall, but the final carveout will need tighter drafting to avoid implementation drift.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to tighten the list and show how it will hold together across programs.
